patch.value:
## Context
Every existing closed item (511 closed Tasks alone; effectively 100% of terminal items across types, verified 2026-07-07) predates a working `closed_at` stamp (defect pm-m4iu). Until they carry `closed_at`, any metadata write on them re-buckets the item into `[Unreleased]` via the `updated_at` fallback — which is exactly what blocks pm-e9zh (close_reason:18 + resolution backfill) and pm-pivf (GH-209 duplicate issue-code rename).

## Derivation (deterministic, no placeholders)
The hash-chained history streams (`.agents/pm/history/<id>.jsonl`) record every mutation as a timestamped JSON-patch op. For each closed item missing `closed_at`:
- `closed_at := ts` of the earliest history entry whose patch puts `status` at closed with no later transition away from closed; for items created already-closed (e.g. pm-2lbp, created 2026-05-01 with closed status), that is the `create` op itself.
- Items whose history is incomplete (pre-history-era or repaired chains) go to a documented residual list instead of receiving a guessed value.

## Delivery
Prefer extending `pm validate --fix-hints` with a closed_at hint plus a new `--auto-fix --fix-scope timestamps` remediation (matches the existing fix-hint machinery; today's hints cover close_reason/title/resolution only). A `pm run normalize` rule is the fallback home. The backfill write is an ordinary history-recorded mutation, so the immutable-proof chain stays intact; the assigned value must equal what history replay yields.

## Ordering
Run only after pm-m4iu ships (otherwise newly closed items regress immediately) and regenerate + review the changelog in the same commit as the first bulk pass. Once complete, pm-e9zh and pm-pivf become executable without `[Unreleased]` churn.
Deterministic closed_at backfill for legacy closed items derived from history streams
Backfill closed_at on all legacy terminal items from their history streams so closed items stop bucketing by updated_at.

validate emits a fix hint for closed items missing closed_at; auto-fix (new timestamps fix-scope) populates closed_at solely from history-replay evidence and is idempotent; items with unrecoverable history land on a documented residual list with counts; changelog regenerated in the same commit as the bulk pass shows zero unintended [Unreleased] churn

value.text:
Unblocked 2026-07-26. The constraint that held this item was that a metadata write on a long-closed item re-buckets it into the current changelog section, because attribution resolved through closed_at ?? updated_at ?? created_at and 1,488 of 1,795 terminal items carried no closed_at. That is no longer true.

Every terminal item now carries a release identifier derived from the tag whose window contains its close event, taken from its immutable history stream: 1,782 stamped, 13 deliberately left unstamped because they close after the newest tag and therefore belong to the pending window. The derivation was validated against ground truth before any write — for the 307 items that already had closed_at, the history-derived instant matched on 307 and disagreed on 0.

The generator honours the release field as the attribution authority under --all-release-tags, which was proved directly rather than assumed: stamping a closed item, which moved its updated_at to now, produced a byte-identical CHANGELOG.md. After the full backfill, regeneration moved 295 items and every one of those moves matched the derivation, with no items added or removed and the Unreleased section unchanged.

The practical consequence for this item: the backfill work it describes can now proceed as ordinary mutations without changelog churn, and the ordering constraint that deferred it no longer applies. Evidence and method are recorded on pm-3j6it6.

value.text: Unblocked and re-scoped 2026-07-31. The declared blocker pm-m4iu (closed_at lifecycle stamping) closed 2026-07-10 with closed_at present, so this backfill has been executable for 21 days; the stale blocked_by edge is retired and priority raised to P1. Fresh measurement: 1,488 of 1,904 terminal items carry neither closed_at nor completed_at (78.2 percent), so the pm-changelog precedence chain completed_at -> closed_at -> updated_at resolves their release section from a mutable field. Consequence recorded as typed edges rather than prose: pm-lnrk, pm-e9zh, pm-pivf, pm-hnc9w7, pm-s5e04g, pm-ye46ns and pm-1w6scp are all blocked_by this item, because each mutates terminal items and would re-bucket them into the current release. This is the single largest unlock in the backlog: it is what the create-only-on-closed-items convention is standing in for, and that convention is why the terminal ordering spine is still 87.7 percent frontier.
